answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with slow-earned identity: a new identity starts with no spending power and must accumulate a public history of useful, verified work - a jade seal only time and honest effort can polish. An agent may wander across many tasks, but each job adds a small, timestamped attestation from independent peers, and trust rises only gradually, like a rising tide. Ten thousand fresh identities buy nothing on day one: each must earn its reputation separately, so attacker cost multiplies with every fake identity while honest agents keep the trust they built.
